title: Comparator-boundary adapter for whole-space R3 Theorem 1.1
intent: Re-expose the project's internal whole-space Theorem 1.1 under the reference Comparator's exact quantifiers and decay predicates, so a comparator client calls `navier_stokes_breakdown_R3` and never unfolds the internal `ProblemStatement`.

parent.name: navier_stokes_breakdown_R3
parent.statement:
theorem navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 (ν : ℝ) (hν : ν > 0) :
    ∃ (u₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
      (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)),
      Comparator.InitialVelocityConditionDecay u₀ ∧ Comparator.ForceConditionDecay f ∧
      ¬ (∃ v p, Comparator.NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn ν u₀ f v p)

children.name: theorem_1_1
children.closed_by: intro ν hν; obtain ⟨u, p, f, K, hc, hg, _⟩ := theorem_1_1_with_initial_rest ν hν; exact ⟨u, p, f, K, hc, hg⟩
children.note: Fully qualified `NavierStokesR3.theorem_1_1`; the project's internal headline result, stated over the internal `ProblemStatement.breakdownStatement` bundle rather than the comparator's predicates. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: The internal whole-space Theorem 1.1: for every positive viscosity there is a candidate whose prescribed force and zero datum admit no global finite-energy solution.

children.name: comparator_of_breakdown
children.statement:
theorem comparator_of_breakdown {ν : ℝ}
    {u : VelocityField} {p : PressureField} {f : VelocityField} {K : Set Space}
    (h : CandidateProperties ν u p f K)
    (hglobal : ¬ Nonempty (GlobalFiniteEnergySolution ν f)) :
    ∃ (u₀ : Space → Space) (f : Space → ℝ → Space),
      NavierStokes.Comparator.InitialVelocityConditionDecay u₀ ∧
      NavierStokes.Comparator.ForceConditionDecay f ∧
      ¬ (∃ v p, NavierStokes.Comparator.NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn ν u₀ f v p)
children.closed_by: refine ⟨fun _ => 0, toComparator f, zero_initial_condition_decay, forceConditionDecay_of_compact h.force_smooth h.force_support.1, ?_⟩; rintro ⟨v, q, hv⟩; exact hglobal ⟨globalSolutionOfComparator hv⟩
children.note: Fully qualified `NavierStokesR3.comparator_of_breakdown`; the conversion lemma that turns the internal `CandidateProperties` plus the absence of a `GlobalFiniteEnergySolution` into the comparator's `InitialVelocityConditionDecay`, `ForceConditionDecay` and `NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn` conclusion. Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: Given candidate properties and the absence of a global finite-energy solution, produce the comparator witness with the decay conditions.

applicability.goal_shape: A project-internal theorem proved over an internal vocabulary (a `ProblemStatement` bundle of predicates such as `CandidateProperties` and `GlobalFiniteEnergySolution`) must be re-stated under an external reference's exact quantifiers and predicate names (here `Comparator.InitialVelocityConditionDecay`, `Comparator.ForceConditionDecay`, `Comparator.NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn`, over `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`).
applicability.use_when: a harness or challenge grader expects the conclusion in its own predicate vocabulary; the internal statement is a structure bundle that clients would otherwise have to unfold; the adapter's proof is pure plumbing — obtain the internal witness, then apply one conversion lemma.
applicability.avoid_when: the two vocabularies are not inter-derivable by a single conversion lemma, so each field needs its own proof; the adapter would need nontrivial mathematics, in which case the conversion lemma is the real content and should be stated and named separately; the boundary changes often, so the adapter must be updated in lockstep with the reference.

consequences: The move splits the work into two named lemmas: the internal theorem (which carries the mathematics) and the conversion lemma (which carries the vocabulary translation). The adapter itself is then trivial — two lines — and stays in sync for free, but any change to either the internal `CandidateProperties`/`GlobalFiniteEnergySolution` or the comparator's `Comparator.*` predicates silently breaks the glue. The comparator's decay predicates are strictly stronger than the internal whole-space conditions, so the real work hides inside the conversion lemma (`forceConditionDecay_of_compact`, `zero_initial_condition_decay`), not in the adapter.
